sections.name: checkCricketContract
sections.title: Cricket match checks
sections.what: Checks each innings for out-of-order deliveries, too many legal balls in an over or the innings, more than ten wickets, and negative runs. Also checks that the winner and any tie agree with the totals. Rain-affected, short, or no-result matches are not violations, but they are marked as not usable for the chase model.
sections.why: Likely reason: bad data must be caught before the model uses it, and marginal matches are kept out without being thrown away.
sections.watch_out: The winner check is skipped when rain revised the match, and the 20 over default fits only Twenty20.

summary: Checks a cricket match's data for errors and decides whether it may feed the win probability model.
purpose: A quality gate for cricket data.
why: Likely reason: bad scores would create false swings in the model.
how: 1. Group deliveries by innings. 2. Check order, legal balls per over and per innings, wickets, and negative runs. 3. Check the winner and any tie against the totals. 4. Collect reasons a match should not feed the model.
inputs: A parsed cricket event and a maximum number of overs (default 20).
outputs: A pass or fail flag, a list of violations, a flag for model use, and a list of reasons.
risks: The default of 20 overs fits Twenty20 only. The winner check is skipped for matches revised by rain.
debug: Read the violations first. Reasons explain why a match is excluded without marking it wrong.
